players.product: MachXO5-NX control FPGAs and Mach-NX / MachXO3D hardware root-of-trust (PFR) FPGAs on server boards

quarterly_data.signal: Record second-quarter revenue of $201 million, up 18% sequentially and 62% year-over-year with strength across all end markets, exceeding the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.53 grew more than 120% year-over-year and 29% quarter-over-quarter. Non-GAAP gross margin was 71.7%, up 170 basis points sequentially and 240 basis points year-over-year on favorable product and customer mix; non-GAAP operating expense $67.1 million; non-GAAP operating margin 38.3% and EBITDA margin 43%. Free cash flow was $81.3 million, a 40.4% margin.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $201 million (+18% QoQ, +62% YoY); non-GAAP EPS $0.53; gross margin 71.7%; operating margin 38.3%; free cash flow $81.3 million

quarterly_data.signal: Third-quarter guidance (FPGA business plus about two months of AMI after the late-July close): FPGA revenue $210 million to $230 million, about 65% year-over-year growth at the $220 million midpoint; AMI revenue $33 million to $37 million; total revenue $245 million to $265 million ($255 million midpoint, which CEO said puts Lattice at over a $1 billion annualized run rate). FPGA gross margin 70% plus or minus 1% as supply-chain cost pressure increases; corporate non-GAAP gross margin 69.5% plus or minus 1% (reflecting transitory AMI items); non-GAAP operating expense $83 million to $90 million; tax rate 4% to 6%; non-GAAP EPS $0.54 to $0.58, midpoint $0.56 or roughly 100% year-over-year growth.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $245 million to $265 million (FPGA $210 million to $230 million, AMI $33 million to $37 million); EPS $0.54 to $0.58; gross margin 69.5% plus or minus 1%

quarterly_data.signal: Long-term aspiration: CEO said the goal is $3 billion of revenue by 2030 and Lattice is already about a quarter ahead — the $1 billion run rate targeted for Q4 was reached in the Q3 guide with AMI — and it should exit 2026 at about a $1.2 billion run rate. CFO: the near-term model holds for now; into 2027 he expects 70-ish percent gross margin and reaching 40% operating margin a little sooner than previously expected, with EPS growth significantly outpacing revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: $3 billion revenue goal by 2030; about $1.2 billion exit run rate for 2026; 70-ish percent gross margin, 40% operating margin

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog and visibility: CEO cited accelerated bookings and backlog extending well into 2027; visibility is 'really unprecedented', reaching the end of 2027, and '2027 is pretty much booked.' Lattice is putting capacity agreements in place with suppliers where it must take the capacity, and in turn capacity agreements with customers and partners so they provide the same commitments. Design win momentum remains healthy across the FPGA portfolio.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog extending well into 2027; 2027 pretty much booked

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: CEO said front-end fab and back-end test supply is fine, but assembly is constrained across the industry; Lattice is putting capacity agreements in place and qualifying new capacity it believes will bring supply and demand in line by September, in good shape in Q4 and definitely for 2027. Costs are rising across the industry, including expedite fees as customers push for supply; Lattice will absorb some and pass some on. CFO: the channel, now at about two months of inventory, is being used to help ensure supply to customers.
quarterly_data.figure: assembly constraints; supply and demand in line by September; channel inventory about two months

quarterly_data.signal: Comms and Compute reached another record, growing 18% sequentially and 83% year-over-year on data center AI momentum. CEO: demand is driven by rising capex, more AI content per server, expanding FPGA attach rates, rising security requirements and more complex disaggregated architectures; attach rates, capex and ASPs of new products (with more complex security) keep rising. The FPGAs' low latency, determinism, parallel processing and wide-range 1.2 to 3.3 volt I/O connect up to 1,200 sensors on some servers, and are finding new uses such as power and cooling. AI-related revenue (systems with GPUs, CPUs or XPUs) is on track to meet or exceed 25% of revenue in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Comms and Compute +18% QoQ, +83% YoY; AI-related revenue on track to meet or exceed 25%; up to 1,200 sensors per server

quarterly_data.signal: Traditional CPU servers: CEO said CPU has been a very strong growth driver with traditional servers and the server business is growing faster than the 83% of Comms and Compute overall, as the agentic revolution drives traditional server, networking, storage and memory infrastructure alongside AI servers; he cited a Digitimes forecast of 20 million server units for 2026. CFO: attach rate is also growing in traditional servers — one CPU can be multiple FPGAs in the infrastructure supporting AI.
quarterly_data.figure: server growth above 83%; 20 million server units forecast for 2026 (Digitimes, cited by CEO)

quarterly_data.signal: Industrial and Embedded revenue rose 17% sequentially and 36% year-over-year (CEO said 16% sequential in the Q&A), with momentum in industrial automation, aerospace and defense, medical, robotics and humanoids, autonomous vehicles and other physical AI applications; channel inventory is at healthy levels and new design wins are ramping. CEO noted a temporary slowdown in China; CFO said automotive is a relatively small business, so its weakness is not a drag, and that I&E has been lumpy but the trend is up.

New products: CEO said new products will exceed the high end of the guided 20% to 25% range, above 25% of total revenue this year, contributing across Compute and Comms and Industrial and Embedded. He described the company as at a 'Rule of 105' (growth rate plus EBITDA margin).

AMI acquisition closed (July 27): combines Lattice low-power FPGAs with AMI boot firmware and infrastructure manageability to build what CEO calls the industry's most complete secure management and control platform for AI data center infrastructure; management expects the combination can double the addressable market and has engaged about 100 hyperscalers, OEMs, ODMs and ecosystem partners with positive feedback. AMI revenue is about 60% boot firmware and 40% infrastructure manageability, from firmware licensing, recurring maintenance and subscription, per-unit royalties and platform enablement services; it will stay silicon-neutral. Management expects AMI to exit 2026 at a revenue run rate of more than $200 million with gross margins above 75% and EBITDA margins above 40%.
quarterly_data.figure: AMI exit-2026 run rate more than $200 million; gross margin above 75%; EBITDA margin above 40%; about 60% boot firmware / 40% manageability

quarterly_data.signal: AMI outlook: CFO expects AMI to grow about 25% in 2027 over the $200 million base, which excludes a low-margin hardware pass-through business AMI began divesting before the deal and expects to fully exit by the end of 2026 (it is in Q3 and Q4 revenue and lowers the Q3 margin). CEO: the 25% excludes revenue synergies, which he expects on top; meaningful EPS accretion is expected from Q4. From the next report FPGA and AMI will be reported as separate segments with revenue and gross margin, keeping the Comms and Compute / Industrial and Embedded split within FPGA.
quarterly_data.figure: AMI growth about 25% in 2027 over $200 million; EPS accretion from Q4
